items.title: Sphere application of Proposition 3.61 · the induced gradient

source.anchor: Boumal 2023 pre-publication annotations through2026-10-08, §3.7 Def3.55 and §3.8 Def3.58/(3.34), (3.36)–(3.39), Prop3.61 and Example3.62 sphere tangent space; printed41–44/PDF57–60
source.attribution: Nicolas Boumal. ASTIS attributed restatement. This is the explicit sphere application of the existing general projection source result, not a new source proposition.

items.statement: Let M be a Riemannian submanifold of a Euclidean space E with the metric induced by E, and let F:M→ℝ be smooth. Its Riemannian gradient is characterized by DF(x)[v]=⟨v,grad F(x)⟩x for every tangent vector v. For any smooth ambient neighborhood extension f of F, grad F(x)=Proj_x(grad f(x)). For the unit sphere the tangent space at x is the orthogonal complement of the line spanned by x.

formulae.label: Actual sphere adapter
formulae.tex: T_xS=(\mathbb R x)^\perp,\quad A_x=D\iota(x),\quad DF(x)[w]=\langle A_xw,P_{T_xS}g\rangle_E.

assumptions: Finite-dimensional real Euclidean space and embedded submanifold with exactly the induced metric.
Smooth real-valued manifold objective and a smooth ambient neighborhood extension.
For the selected application M is the unit sphere with the inherited metric; Example3.56/3.62 supplies this source specialization.

obligations.label: Construct and uniquely characterize the tangent projection for the actual unit-sphere manifold differential.
General embedded-manifold differential/tangent/induced metric and arbitrary neighborhood-extension adapter remain separate.
Global smooth metric/gradient field and full source vector-field construction remain separate.

bindings.boundary: Unit-sphere specialization with true Mathlib manifold differential and ambient tangent representation using actual inclusion derivative; pointwise ambient HasGradientAt generalizes smoothness. No general embedded-manifold theorem, chosen default chart metric identification, global smooth field, general neighborhood extension construction or Rayleigh quotient computation. No global Riemannian metric typeclass or smooth-field construction is certified by the pointwise pairing.
